"4e75bdad-f36e-527c-a1e9-527d230dfe09" :question/math-academy-id "q-79748" :question/problem "Given a rectangular solid, find the differential $\text{d}S$ for the surface area $S$ of the rectangular solid if the lengths of the sides are $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=7.$" :question/worked-solution "The  surface area of the rectangular solid is $S=2ab+2bc+2ac.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}S(a,b,c) & =(\frac{∂S}{∂a})\,\text{d}a+(\frac{∂S}{∂b})\,\text{d}b+(\frac{∂S}{∂c})\,\text{d}c \\  & =2(b+c)\,\text{d}a+2(a+c)\,\text{d}b+2(a+b)\,\text{d}c\end{aligned}
$$

For $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=7,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}S(4,5,7) & =2(5+7)\,\text{d}a+2(4+7)\,\text{d}b+2(4+5)\,\text{d}c \\  & =24\,\text{d}a+22\,\text{d}b+18\,\text{d}c.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-91bbad55-b7c9-5018-bd2b-a6b22c055c21"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-91bbad55-b7c9-5018-bd2b-a6b22c055c21" :answer-field/id #uuid "91bbad55-b7c9-5018-bd2b-a6b22c055c21" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-15f3dee8-e6f4-5787-8395-50cb7a5ce3d9" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a1659264-c9c8-589f-9fdb-0ef010eb62c1" "answer-15f3dee8-e6f4-5787-8395-50cb7a5ce3d9" "answer-1cbc47ca-c217-5961-8ebc-60818e4b7533" "answer-8596556d-0399-5275-8336-5e8a62170257" "answer-418af1c1-d6d4-51bf-ada3-9317c8a8af10"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a1659264-c9c8-589f-9fdb-0ef010eb62c1" :answer/id #uuid "a1659264-c9c8-589f-9fdb-0ef010eb62c1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12\,\text{d}a+11\,\text{d}b+9\,\text{d}c" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-15f3dee8-e6f4-5787-8395-50cb7a5ce3d9" :answer/id #uuid "15f3dee8-e6f4-5787-8395-50cb7a5ce3d9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24\,\text{d}a+22\,\text{d}b+18\,\text{d}c" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1cbc47ca-c217-5961-8ebc-60818e4b7533" :answer/id #uuid "1cbc47ca-c217-5961-8ebc-60818e4b7533" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "35\,\text{d}a+28\,\text{d}b+20\,\text{d}c" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8596556d-0399-5275-8336-5e8a62170257" :answer/id #uuid "8596556d-0399-5275-8336-5e8a62170257" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4\,\text{d}a+5\,\text{d}b+7\,\text{d}c" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-418af1c1-d6d4-51bf-ada3-9317c8a8af10" :answer/id #uuid "418af1c1-d6d4-51bf-ada3-9317c8a8af10" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8\,\text{d}a+10\,\text{d}b+14\,\text{d}c" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186125814 :tutorial/content "Given a multivariable function $f(x,y),$ the differential

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

tells us how infinitesimal changes in $x$ and $y,$ denoted $\textrm dx$ and $\textrm dy,$ result in an infinitesimal change in $f,$ denoted $\textrm df.$

Consequently, we can use the differential to *approximate* the change in $f$ as we move from one point to another. If we move from a point $(x,y)$ to a point $(x + \Delta x, y + \Delta y),$ then the approximate change in $f$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf(x,y) & ≈(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,Δx+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,Δy.\end{aligned}
$$

The above formula is very similar to the differential formula, except the $\textrm d$'s are replaced with $\Delta$'s. The $\textrm d$'s refer to infinitesimal changes, while the $\Delta$'s refer to changes that can actually be measured." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124739 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf(x,y) & ≈(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,Δx+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,Δy.\end{aligned}
$$

The above formula is very similar to the differential formula, except the $\textrm d$'s are replaced with $\Delta$'s.
